{{Infobox religious building|image=File:Migukurumitama jinja shimohaiden.jpg|prefecture={{ill|Tondabayashi|qid=Q490928}}|coordinates={{Coord|34.51797222222222|N|135.60141666666667}}}}{
'''Migukurumitama Shrine''' (美具久留御魂神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Tondabayashi|en|Tondabayashi|qid=Q490928|lt=Tondabayashi}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}. It is an {{ill|historic shrine|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} and was formerly Ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} under the [[modern shrine Ranking system]]. The shrine is also selected as one of the {{ill|100 Green Selections of Osaka|ja|100 Greens of Ōsaka}}.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pref.osaka.lg.jp/midorikikaku/toshiryokka/hyakusenn.html|title=Osaka 100 Green Selections|publisher=Osaka Prefecture|accessdate=2016-12-23}}</ref> It is also referred to as the "Shimono Suibun Shrine" (下水分社) and, along with {{ill|Tatsuta Shrine|ja|建水分神社}} (the Kamisuibun Shrine in {{ill|Chihayaakasaka|en|Chihayaakasaka|qid=Q1072574|lt=Chihayaakasaka}}) and {{ill|Nishikori Shrine|ja|錦織神社}} (in Tondabayashi), it is one of the "Three Mikumari Shrines of {{ill|Kawachi Province|be|Каваты (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Kawachi|ckb|پارێزگای کاواچی|cs|Provincie Kawači|de|Provinz Kawachi|es|Provincia de Kawachi|fa|ولایت کاواچی|fr|Province de Kawachi|gl|Provincia de Kawachi|hak|Kawachi-koet|id|Provinsi Kawachi|it|Kawachi (provincia)|ja|河内国|ko|가와치국|lt|Kavačio žemė|nl|Kawachi (provincie)|pt|Província de Kawachi|ru|Кавати (провинция)|simple|Kawachi Province|sk|Kawači (provincia)|sr|Провинција Кавачи|tr|Kawachi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Каваті|zh|河內國|zh_min_nan|Kawati-kok|zh_yue|河內國|qid=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi Province}}."
== Enshrined Deities ==  
* '''Primary Deity:''' Migukurumitama no Ōkami (美具久留御魂大神) – The {{ill|Mitama|en|Mitama|qid=Q495568|lt=Aramitama}} (rough spirit) of {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944}}. It is believed to represent a water deity, deriving its name from "Mikukurumitama" (Water Swimming Spirit).  
* '''Additional Deities:'''  
** {{ill|Mikumari|fr|Mikumari|ja|天水分神|lt=Amemikumari no Kami}} (Heavenly Mikumari Deity)  
** {{ill|Mizuhanome|ja|弥都波迺売命|lt=Mizuhanome no Mikoto}}  
** {{ill|Mikumari|fr|Mikumari|ja|国水分神|lt=Kuni no Mikumari no Kami}}  
** {{ill|Suseri-Hime|ja|須勢理比売命|lt=Suseribime no Mikoto}}  
** {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|木花咲耶比売神}}
== History ==  
=== Foundation ===  
According to tradition, the shrine was founded in the 10th year of Emperor Sujin's reign (88 BCE). A giant serpent frequently appeared in the area, leading the emperor to identify it as the aramitama of Ōkuninushi. He dispatched {{ill|Izumo no Furune|ja|出雲振根}} to enshrine the deity, borrowing sacred objects from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|ja|杵築大社|lt=Izumo Taisha}}.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Japanese Place Name Dictionary|publisher=Heibonsha|year=1986}}</ref>  
In Emperor Sujin's 62nd year, an oracle declared that "Mikukurumitama" should be the deity's name, and the shrine was established to house this deity alongside four others.  
=== Historical Records ===  
The shrine may correspond to the "Kawachi Province Wani Shrine" mentioned in 850 CE, where the deity's Rank was raised to {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|ja|従五位上|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade}}. During the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, it also served as a clan shrine for the {{ill|Kusunoki clan|ja|楠木氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki family|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11541208}}, who venerated the shrine as their ancestral deity.  
The shrine was burned down during the {{ill|Siege of Akasaka|en|Siege of Akasaka|qid=Q7509791|lt=Siege of Akasaka}} in 1331 but was later rebuilt under the support of {{ill|Kusunoki Masashige|en|Kusunoki Masashige|qid=Q382234|lt=Kusunoki Masashige}}. In 1585, it was again destroyed during the {{ill|Battle of Kishuu|ja|紀州征伐|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kishū Campaign|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10855721}} by {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|af|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|ar|تويوتومي هيده-يوشي|arz|تويوتومى هيده يوشى|ast|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|az|Toyotomi Hideyoşi|ban|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|be|Таётомі Хідэёсі|bg|Тойотоми Хидейоши|ca|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|cdo|Hŭng-sìng Séu-gék|ckb|تۆیۆتۆمی ھیدێیۆشی|cs|Hidejoši Tojotomi|de|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|el|Τογιοτόμι Χιντεγιόσι|eo|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|es|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|et|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|eu|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|fa|تویوتومی هیده‌یوشی|fi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|fr|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|gl|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|glk|تویوتومی هیده یوشی|hak|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|he|טויוטומי הידיושי|hr|Tojotomi Hidejoši|hu|Tojotomi Hidejosi|hy|Տոյոտոմի Հիդեյոսի|ia|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|id|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|is|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|it|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|ja|豊臣秀吉|ka|ტოიოტომი ჰიდეიოსი|kk|Тоётоми Хидэёси|ko|도요토미 히데요시|kw|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|la|Taicosama|lt|Tojotomi Hidejoši|lv|Tojotomi Hidejosi|mg|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|ml|തൊയൊത്തോമി ഹിദെയോഷി|ms|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|nl|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|no|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|oc|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|pl|Hideyoshi Toyotomi|pt|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|ro|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|ru|Тоётоми Хидэёси|sc|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|sco|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|simple|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|sk|Hidejoši Tojotomi|sl|Tojotomi Hidejoši|sq|Tojotomi Hidejoshi|sr|Тојотоми Хидејоши|sv|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|tg|Тайетоми Хидзеси|th|โทโยโตมิ ฮิเดโยชิ|tl|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|tr|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|uk|Тойотомі Хідейосі|ur|تویوتومی ہیدیئوشی|vi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|war|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|wuu|丰臣秀吉|zh|丰臣秀吉|zh_classical|豐臣秀吉|zh_min_nan|Toyotomi Hideyosi|zh_yue|豐臣秀吉|zu|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|qid=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}}. The current main shrine was reconstructed in 1660.  
The shrine was designated as a gōsha in 1872 during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}.  
== Shrine Grounds ==  
The shrine grounds include the following structures:  
* '''Main Shrine (Honden):''' Rebuilt in 1660.  
* '''Upper Worship Hall (Kami-haiden):''' Rebuilt in 1660.  
* '''Lower Worship Hall (Shimo-haiden):'''  
* '''Treasure Hall (Saigu-kura):'''  
* '''Gates and Torii:'''  
* '''Miyajinja Uramayama Kofun Group:''' Includes a keyhole-shaped kofun (58 m long) believed to be from the early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Uramayama Kofun Explanation Board|publisher=Educational Board of Tondabayashi|accessdate=2020-08-28}}</ref>
